name: Lesson 36 · Trying to, in order to: the infinitive with zu, um … zu

cards.note: The infinitive with zu. After many verbs a second verb takes zu and goes to the very end.
The infinitive with zu. With a separable verb, zu goes between the prefix and the stem: anzurufen, one word.

cards.front: Don't forget **to water** the flowers! (one friend)
cards.note: The infinitive with zu. vergessen + zu-infinitive. gießen: to water.
The infinitive with zu. Zeit haben, Lust haben + zu: zu kochen at the end.

cards.front: Do you feel like **going out**? (one friend)
cards.note: The infinitive with zu. ausgehen → auszugehen: zu in the middle.
The infinitive with zu. English often uses -ing where German uses zu + infinitive.

cards.front: Do you have time **to help** me? (one friend)
cards.note: The infinitive with zu. Everything else of the zu clause comes before zu helfen.
The infinitive with zu. Es ist + adjective + zu-infinitive. Sport machen: to do sport.

cards.front: It isn't easy **to learn** a language.
cards.back: Es ist nicht leicht, eine Sprache **zu lernen**.
cards.note: The infinitive with zu. leicht: easy. The zu-infinitive closes the sentence.
The infinitive with zu. aufstehen → aufzustehen.
The infinitive with zu. verboten: forbidden.
The infinitive with zu. möglich + zu-infinitive.
The infinitive with zu. aufhören + zu: to stop doing something.
The infinitive with zu. anfangen + zu-infinitive.

cards.back: Ich habe vor, meine Oma **zu besuchen**.
cards.note: The infinitive with zu. vorhaben: to plan. habe … vor, then the zu clause.
The infinitive with zu. früher: earlier. aufzustehen, one word.
The infinitive with zu. einkaufen → einzukaufen.

cards.front: It was my plan **to arrive** early.
cards.note: The infinitive with zu. ankommen → anzukommen.
The infinitive with zu. After a modal there is no zu: will lernen, never will zu lernen.

cards.front: I'm learning German **in order to** work in Germany.
cards.back: Ich lerne Deutsch, **um** in Deutschland **zu** arbeiten.
cards.note: um … zu: in order to. um … zu says the purpose: um opens the clause, zu + infinitive closes it.
um … zu: in order to. English to = um … zu when it means in order to.
um … zu: in order to. um … zu bleiben: in order to stay.

cards.front: I'm getting up early **to** catch the train.
cards.back: Ich stehe früh auf, **um** den Zug **zu** erreichen.
cards.note: um … zu: in order to. den Zug erreichen: to catch the train.

cards.front: She's going to the bakery **to** buy bread.
cards.back: Sie geht zur Bäckerei, **um** Brot **zu** kaufen.
cards.note: um … zu: in order to. um … zu kaufen: to buy.

cards.front: **To** pass the exam, you have to study a lot. (one friend)
cards.back: **Um** die Prüfung **zu** bestehen, musst du viel lernen.
cards.note: um … zu: in order to. The um clause takes the first place, so musst comes straight after the comma.

cards.back: Ich rufe an, **um** einen Termin **zu** machen.
cards.note: um … zu: in order to. einen Termin machen: to make an appointment.

cards.front: We're going into town **to do the shopping**.
cards.back: Wir fahren in die Stadt, **um einzukaufen**.
cards.note: um … zu: in order to. With a separable verb, zu sits inside it: um einzukaufen.

cards.front: He's learning English **to** get a new job.
cards.back: Er lernt Englisch, **um** einen neuen Job **zu** bekommen.
cards.note: um … zu: in order to. um … zu bekommen: in order to get.

cards.front: He works a lot **to** save money.
cards.note: um … zu: in order to. sparen: to save money.

cards.front: I don't have enough money **to** buy a car.
cards.back: Ich habe nicht genug Geld, **um** ein Auto **zu** kaufen.
cards.note: um … zu: in order to. genug … um … zu: enough … to.
